canvas-uniform-scalingscene-fixed-canvas-uniform-fit0.75 of 0.75 (major)passuseFitScale measures the stage element&#39;s own bounding rect, on resize and via ResizeObserver. computeFitScale takes one scale = min((w-2*insetX)/880, (h-2*insetY)/380, maxScale), floored at MIN_SCALE. Stage applies that single value as transform scale(s) to a fixed 880×380 canvas centered in the stage, which has overflow hidden. At 1280×720 (browse) the stage is roughly 1100 px wide, so width gives about 1.2; the height of roughly 500 px gives about 1.25, so the scale is about 1.2 and the canvas is about 1060×460, within the stage. At 390×844 in browse mode the Toc is hidden, the stage is 390 px wide, and the scale is (390-48)/880 ≈ 0.39, giving a canvas about 342 px wide. This is above MIN_SCALE, so the floor is not reached. The fit is computed from the stage&#39;s own box, not the window, so it accounts for the rendered chrome.fit.ts computeFitScale: one scale for both axes, using the mode&#39;s insets and maxScale | useFitScale.ts: getBoundingClientRect of the viewport ref plus a resize listener and ResizeObserver | Stage.tsx: viewport ref on [data-presentation-stage]; the canvas has transform `translate(-50%,-50%) scale(${scale})` with a fixed width and height | motion-wiring.test.tsx &#39;stage geometry&#39;: scale = 952/880 at 1000 wide, 452/880 after a resize to 500, 968/880 in present mode, with constant canvas dimensions | judging basis: consensus-pass | src/presentation-kit/fit.ts | src/presentation-kit/useFitScale.ts | src/presentation-kit/Stage.tsx | src/presentation-kit/constants.ts | src/tests/motion-wiring.test.tsx | src/tests/fit.test.ts

None of them calls Playwright directly or sleeps. Each one spawns `npm run verify` or `npm run inspect` through helpers.mjs run(), waits for the process to close, and only then asserts on the exit code, output, files and leftover processes. Every browser step wait those runs rely on is a polling wait on observable state. verify.mjs calls waitForStepIndex (verify-lib.mjs), which uses page.waitForFunction on data-step-index with a timeout, before it reads the title, caption and era. Inspect&#39;s goTo presses ArrowRight and then runs page.waitForFunction on data-step-index before captureSteps continues. Inspect first waits for the selector, then reads data-step-count. The only setTimeout in helpers.mjs is a SIGKILL watchdog, not a wait before an assertion. Judge C&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. The fixed settle interval (page.waitForTimeout in the inspect script, used by captureSteps) runs only after goTo has already confirmed the step index. So it is not a fixed sleep used in place of waiting for a transition. INT-002 passes `--settle 2000` to measure that settle feature, which is a fixed post-arrival delay before each screenshot, not something the tests use to wait for state before asserting. The guidance&#39;s fail case, a fixed wait for a transition before asserting the step, does not occur. Judges A and B correctly found no fixed sleeps standing in for state waits.","evidence":["tests/integration/helpers.mjs run() resolves on child &#39;close&#39;. The only tests that drive a browser are the four files under tests/integration, which vitest.integration.config.ts collects and describes as the browser-backed suites. vitest.config.ts runs every src/** test in jsdom, so none of those drives a browser. The integration files are quoted in full. None calls waitForTimeout, a sleep or Playwright directly. Each one runs `npm run verify` or `npm run inspect` through run() in helpers.mjs, which awaits the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event before resolving. Its only setTimeout is a SIGKILL watchdog, not a wait for state. The browser waits come from the scripts these tests run, and they poll observable state. verify presses ArrowRight, then waitForStepIndex polls data-step-index with page.waitForFunction and a timeout before it reads the title, caption or era. It also waits for the [data-step-count] selector before reading the count. In inspect, goTo presses ArrowRight and polls data-step-index with waitForFunction before the settle wait and the capture. inspect also waits for [data-step-count] before reading the count. Judge A and Judge B said pass, and the quoted material bears out their reasons. Judge C said fail because INT-002 runs inspect with --settle 2000 and inspect&#39;s wait uses page.waitForTimeout. That observation is accurate but does not decide the requirement. The requirement is broken only when a test sleeps for a fixed time instead of waiting for state. In captureSteps, goTo(index) runs before wait(settleMs), and goTo in inspect-presentation.mjs already blocks on waitForFunction until data-step-index equals the target. The settle interval is an extra pause after a state-based wait, so it does not stand in for one. verify&#39;s waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS) likewise runs only after waitForStepIndex and the assertions. The guidance also says longer fixed settle delays are not scored.
